title: review and restructure quest help/instructions for agent discoverability -- sharp edges are documented but buried in long prose, some flags are undiscoverable without probing
description:
Raised by opum-agent, relaying the user's own words directly (not paraphrased): "make sure the help and instructions are fully reviewed and updated so that the actual agents know how to use the functionality properly." Dispatched 2026-09-18 12:44Z with the user's approval.

opum-agent's evidence, from driving quest all day as a fresh caller, offered as symptoms rather than a spec:
1. `quest help` prints the full command registry as YAML with multi-paragraph summaries -- complete but nearly unskimmable; some single command summaries run a dozen lines. opum-agent resorted to grep instead of reading it.
2. Sharp edges are documented only inside those long summaries, easy to miss: checklist positions are 1-based and reader-facing (QCLI-269, QCLI-315 already fixed the substance -- this is about whether the fact surfaces skimmably); `--comments`/`--add-comment` need structured JSON objects, not free text; `task pause` is the only way in and `task start` the only way out of the paused status.
3. Things opum-agent had to discover by probing rather than reading: that `task create` accepts `--description` at all, and the exact spelling of the actor/actor-kind/accountable-human triple.

Related prior work, already Done, that narrowed but did not close this: QCLI-127 (help prints raw manifest instead of human-readable text), QCLI-266 (help/manifest silent on how to write a valid task create), QCLI-128 (an earlier full accuracy/completeness pass over quest instructions output), QCLI-148 (instructions guides' own commands are now tested so a guide cannot ship a broken recipe). This task is a discoverability pass on top of that accuracy work, not a redo of it -- the guides are accurate; the finding is that critical facts are hard to find inside them.

Test for done, per opum-agent: whether an agent that has never used quest can do the right thing without probing -- not whether every fact already exists somewhere in the text.

acceptanceCriteria.text: quest help's output is restructured or supplemented so a first-time caller can find a command's usage without reading a multi-paragraph summary -- e.g. a short usage line separated from extended notes, or a --brief/--full split

The specific sharp edges opum-agent hit (1-based checklist positions, --comments structured-JSON shape, pause/start as the only paused-status entry/exit) are each surfaced somewhere a caller sees before making the mistake, not only inside a long summary paragraph

The two things opum-agent had to discover by probing (--description on task create, the exact actor/actor-kind/accountable-human spelling) are each independently greppable/discoverable from --help output at the command level

The change is validated against the user's own test: have a fresh-context agent attempt a small real task (e.g. create a task with a comment and a checked acceptance criterion) using only quest help/instructions output, with no prior knowledge of quest, and confirm it succeeds without trial-and-error probing
quest instructions --list and the per-guide instructions are cross-checked against this pass so the two surfaces (help vs instructions guides) do not duplicate or contradict each other
